correctness.rationale: For any length-N prefix containing k+1 ones the iterate deletes exactly the first k original ones. Equal images identify the position of the (k+1)st one by the leading zero count and identify the suffix after it. Truncating the originals at N then gives equal prefix images, so injectivity at N forces equality of the originals. For the critical finite checks I used actual factors from the recurrence f(2j)=f(j), f(2j+1)=j mod 2, rather than executing the supplied wildcard code. If P=2^r and n<=P, choose the representative start 1<=a<=2P. All nonexceptional positions are invariant on translating by 2P. The sole multiple of P, if any, has quotient 1 or 2 in that representative window; translating by 2P or 4P respectively gives quotient 3 or 6 and flips its bit. Thus starts 1 through 6P cover every factor. The scan matched all eight counts and collision classes and all four explicit witness starts. At N=13,14,25,26 the respective minima of ones are 5,5,10,11, so the lifting argument applies, and the four predecessor collisions prove sharpness. 'First injective length' in the table means onset of permanent injectivity, not necessarily the first isolated injective length.
residual_risks: The scan certifies the critical lengths only; the all-length result is analytical. No result is audited for k>=6.
